subject.title: v2026.6.x system prompt bloat causes instruction following degradation on smaller models

question: Should OpenClaw address this smaller-model regression by changing default prompt/skill priority and scoping behavior, by keeping lean mode as an opt-in workaround, or by folding it into the broader context-compactor and skill-index roadmap?
rationale: The remaining work crosses prompt priority, skill loading, tool-surface defaults, model capability heuristics, and config compatibility, and source inspection cannot choose that product boundary safely.

options.title: Define prompt priority and scoping policy
options.body: Keep this issue open and use it to drive a maintainer-owned policy for model-aware prompt slimming, skill-content priority, and validation on smaller models.

options.title: Treat lean mode as the supported workaround
options.body: Close only if maintainers explicitly decide opt-in localModelLean plus docs is the intended support boundary for these models.

options.title: Fold into broader compactor work
options.body: Make the context compactor or smart skill-index issue canonical if maintainers want this regression tracked only through that larger feature program.

recommendation.title: Define prompt priority and scoping policy
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and use it to drive a maintainer-owned policy for model-aware prompt slimming, skill-content priority, and validation on smaller models.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest recent history on localModelLean behavior and related local-model docs, making them the best available routing owner for this product choice.
